$comment: Curated VASP / exchange label corpus.
READ THIS BEFORE ADDING ENTRIES.
Every entry asserts that a real company controls a real address. An
investigator may serve a preservation notice on the named VASP because of
it, so a wrong entry is worse than a missing one -- a missing label
degrades to behavioural inference, while a wrong label sends a notice to
the wrong company and wastes the freeze window.
Addresses widely repeated in blog posts and forum answers do NOT survive
checking. During development, four commonly-cited 'exchange hot wallets'
were profiled against the live chain: one showed 0 senders and 198
receivers (a payout wallet, not a deposit target) and two showed retail
activity inconsistent with any exchange. Only one showed genuine
exchange-class behaviour.
So: run `python scripts/vet_labels.py` before committing any entry. It
profiles each address on-chain and reports whether the behaviour is
consistent with the claimed role.
Sourcing that is acceptable:
- the VASP's own published proof-of-reserves or documentation
- an address the VASP confirmed to the team in writing
- a regulator or court filing
- an address the team traced and verified themselves
Sourcing that is NOT acceptable:
- 'seen on a blog', an LLM, or an unsourced GitHub gist
Sanctioned addresses do not belong here. They are ingested from the OFAC
SDN list by scripts/ingest_ofac.py, which is authoritative and dated.
